title: Critere de platitude par fibres, Noetherian case
statement: Let $R$, $S$, $S'$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $R\to S\to S'$ local ring homomorphisms (each maps the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal); let $\mathfrak m\subset R$ be the maximal ideal. Let $M$ be an $S'$-module, regarded as an $S$-module and an $R$-module by restriction of scalars. Assume (1) $M$ is a finitely generated $S'$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (2) $M\neq0$; (3) $M/\mathfrak mM$ is a flat $S/\mathfrak mS$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (4) $M$ is a flat $R$-module. Then $S$ is flat over $R$ and $M$ is a flat $S$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian, line 23978); its proof uses Remark 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal), Lemma 00ML (lemma-variant-local-criterion-flatness), Nakayama's Lemma 00DV, Lemma 00HP (lemma-ff)

proof.text: (Notation.) Write $\varphi:R\to S$ and $\psi:S\to S'$ for the given local homomorphisms, $\mathfrak m_S$, $\mathfrak m_{S'}$ for the maximal ideals of $S$, $S'$, and set $I=\mathfrak mS\subset S$, the ideal generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m)$. Since $\varphi$ is local, $\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$ and $I\neq S$. For $a\in\mathfrak m$, $s\in S$, $x\in M$ one has $(\varphi(a)s)x=a(sx)$, so $IM=\mathfrak mM$ as submodules of $M$; hence $M/IM=M/\mathfrak mM$ with $S/I=S/\mathfrak mS$ acting in the same way, and by hypothesis (3) $M/IM$ is a flat $S/I$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. (Stacks: 'Set $I=\mathfrak mS$. Then $M/IM$ is a flat $S/I$-module because of (3).')

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: (The surjection $\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to I\otimes_SM$.) Let $\mu_R:\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, and $\mu_S:I\otimes_SM\to M$, $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$, be the multiplication maps, and $\alpha:\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to I\otimes_SM$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\varphi(a)\otimes x$ (well defined, as $(a,x)\mapsto\varphi(a)\otimes x$ is $R$-bilinear). Then $\mu_S\circ\alpha=\mu_R$ (check on generators: $\varphi(a)x=ax$). And $\alpha$ is surjective: $I\otimes_SM$ is generated as an abelian group by the elements $b\otimes x$ with $b=\sum_j\varphi(a_j)s_j\in I$ ($a_j\in\mathfrak m$, $s_j\in S$), and $b\otimes x=\sum_j\varphi(a_j)\otimes s_jx=\alpha(\sum_ja_j\otimes s_jx)$ by $S$-bilinearity. (Stacks: 'Since $\mathfrak m\otimes_RS'\to I\otimes_SS'$ is surjective we see that also $\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to I\otimes_SM$ is surjective'; the computation above shows the surjectivity for $M$ directly.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: ($I\otimes_SM\to M$ is injective.) The inclusion $\mathfrak m\to R$ is injective and $M$ is a flat $R$-module by (4), so by the definition of flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] $\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to R\otimes_RM$ is injective; composed with the isomorphism $R\otimes_RM\cong M$, $r\otimes x\mapsto rx$, this is $\mu_R$, so $\mu_R$ is injective. Now if $y\in I\otimes_SM$ has $\mu_S(y)=0$, write $y=\alpha(z)$ (step 2); then $\mu_R(z)=\mu_S(\alpha(z))=0$, so $z=0$ and $y=0$. Hence $\mu_S$ is injective (and $\alpha$ is an isomorphism). (Stacks: 'As $M$ is flat over $R$ the composition is injective and so both arrows are injective. In particular $\mathrm{Tor}_1^S(S/I,M)=0$ see Remark 00M6'; the cited node below is stated directly with the injectivity of $I\otimes_SM\to M$, the kernel which Remark 00M6 identifies with $\mathrm{Tor}_1^S(M,S/I)$, so no Tor is needed.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: ($M$ is flat over $S$.) Apply the variant of the local criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-variant-local-criterion] (Stacks 00ML) to the local homomorphism $\psi:S\to S'$ of Noetherian local rings, the proper ideal $I\subsetneq S$ (step 1) and the finitely generated $S'$-module $M$ (hypothesis (1)), regarded as an $S$-module via $\psi$: its hypothesis (1), the injectivity of $I\otimes_SM\to M$, is step 3, and its hypothesis (2), the flatness of $M/IM$ over $S/I$, is step 1. Hence $M$ is a flat $S$-module. (Stacks: 'By Lemma 00ML we conclude that $M$ is flat over $S$.')

proof.text: ($M$ is faithfully flat over $S$.) $M$ is a flat $S$-module (step 4) and $\mathfrak m_SM\neq M$ for the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ of $S$ (step 5), so $M$ is a faithfully flat $S$-module [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] (Stacks 00HP, (4)$\Rightarrow$(1)). (Stacks: 'we see that actually $M$ is faithfully flat over $S$ by Lemma 00HP'.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MP (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre-Noetherian), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: ($S$ is flat over $R$.) $M$ is an $S$-module which is flat as an $R$-module (hypothesis (4); its $R$-module structure is the one through $\varphi$) and faithfully flat as an $S$-module (step 6). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-permanence] (Stacks 039V) $\varphi:R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Together with step 4 this proves the lemma. (Stacks' second paragraph reaches the same conclusion by computing with $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(\kappa,S)=\ker(\mathfrak m\otimes_RS\to I)$: tensoring $0\to\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(\kappa,S)\to\mathfrak m\otimes_RS\to I\to0$ over $S$ with the flat $M$ and using that $\mathfrak m\otimes_RM\to I\otimes_SM$ is injective (step 3) gives $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(\kappa,S)\otimes_SM=0$, hence $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(\kappa,S)=0$ by faithful flatness, and Lemma 00MK concludes. Lemma 039V packages exactly this descent of injectivity along the faithfully flat $M$, for all injections at once, and is used here in its place, as the lead's plan prescribes.)
